questions.q: What is a landfill?
questions.a: A low-lying open ground where city garbage is dumped and covered with soil layer by layer.

questions.q: What happens to waste in a landfill?
questions.a: It is spread, pressed and covered; biodegradable parts rot slowly over years.

questions.q: Give one problem of landfills near cities.
questions.a: They breed flies and germs, smell bad and pollute air and groundwater.

questions.q: What is composting?
questions.a: Converting biodegradable waste (peels, leaves) into manure by rotting it in a pit.

questions.q: What is compost and how is it useful?
questions.a: Dark, nutrient-rich manure from rotted waste - it enriches soil for plants.

questions.q: Name the waste suitable for composting.
questions.a: Kitchen peels, garden leaves, paper and other plant matter.

questions.q: Which wastes go into the blue bin and the green bin?
questions.a: Blue bin: recyclable wastes (paper, plastic, glass, metal). Green bin: kitchen and plant waste.

questions.q: Why should waste be segregated at source?
questions.a: Sorted waste can be recycled or composted easily; mixed waste ends in landfills.

questions.q: Give two examples of recyclable waste.
questions.a: Newspaper, plastic bottles, glass jars, tin cans.

questions.q: What is vermicomposting?
questions.a: Using redworms to convert kitchen and plant waste into rich compost (vermicompost).

questions.q: Which worms are used in vermicomposting?
questions.a: Redworms (red wrigglers) that eat waste quickly.

questions.q: How is vermicompost better than chemical fertiliser?
questions.a: It is natural, improves soil texture and does not pollute.

questions.q: Describe the body of a redworm that helps it eat waste.
questions.a: A tube-like body with a mouth at one end; food is ground in a gizzard (with small stones).

questions.q: What is the role of the gizzard in a redworm?
questions.a: It grinds the food into small pieces for digestion.

questions.q: Why are redworms called friends of farmers?
questions.a: They turn waste into manure that enriches fields naturally.

questions.q: How is paper recycled?
questions.a: Old paper is soaked, beaten to pulp, cleaned, pressed into sheets and dried.

questions.q: Name two products made from recycled paper.
questions.a: Egg trays, paper bags, packaging boards and fresh newsprint.

questions.q: Why should we recycle paper?
questions.a: Each tonne of recycled paper saves about 17 trees and much water and energy.

questions.q: Why is plastic waste dangerous to animals?
questions.a: Cows and strays swallow plastic bags which choke their stomachs; plastic also blocks drains.

questions.q: Name two ways to reduce plastic waste.
questions.a: Carry cloth bags and refuse single-use plastics; reuse plastic containers.

questions.q: Why does plastic not rot even after years?
questions.a: It is non-biodegradable - microbes cannot digest it, so it piles up for decades.
